questions.question: A stretched elastic band stores energy in which store?
questions.explanation: Stretching or squashing an object fills its elastic store.

questions.question: As a ball rolls down a hill, which store empties and which fills?
questions.explanation: It loses height (gravitational store) and speeds up (kinetic store).

questions.question: Which statement is true?
options: Energy is transferred but the total stays the same
questions.answer: Energy is transferred but the total stays the same
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved: it is only transferred between stores.

questions.question: A light bulb transfers 100 J of energy. 20 J is transferred usefully by light. How much is wasted?
questions.explanation: $100 - 20 = 80$ J is wasted, mostly heating the surroundings.

questions.question: Food labels show energy in which unit?
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in joules; food uses kilojoules (and kilocalories).

questions.question: In a series circuit, one bulb breaks. What happens to the other bulbs?
questions.explanation: A series circuit has one loop; a break stops the current everywhere.

questions.question: What does an ammeter measure?
questions.explanation: An ammeter measures current in amps (A) and is connected in series.

questions.question: How is a voltmeter connected in a circuit?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures potential difference across a component, so it goes in parallel.

questions.question: Two identical bulbs are in parallel. What happens if one is unscrewed?
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch is its own loop, so the other bulb still has a complete circuit.

questions.question: Which material is an electrical insulator?
questions.explanation: Plastic does not let current flow easily. Metals are conductors.

questions.question: Why are fossil fuels described as non-renewable?
options: They take millions of years to form and will run out
questions.answer: They take millions of years to form and will run out
questions.explanation: They form over millions of years, far faster than we use them.

questions.question: Which uses more energy: a 2000 W kettle for 2 minutes or a 10 W lamp for 2 minutes?
questions.explanation: Power is energy per second; the kettle transfers 200 times as much energy each second.
